bulk-processor.q: How many images can I process at once?
bulk-processor.a: There is no hard limit. The tool can comfortably handle 50-200 images on a typical laptop. Performance depends on image size and your browser's available memory. For very large batches (500+ images), consider splitting into smaller batches.

bulk-processor.q: Is there a file size limit per image?
bulk-processor.a: There is no enforced limit, but images over 50 MB may slow down processing. For best performance, we recommend images under 20 MB each.

bulk-processor.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
bulk-processor.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your computer — 100% private and secure.

bulk-processor.q: Can I rename output files in batch?
bulk-processor.a: Yes! The batch rename feature lets you set a prefix followed by auto-incrementing numbers (e.g. product_001.jpg, product_002.jpg). You can also keep original filenames by leaving the rename option off.
You can output as JPG, PNG, WebP, or keep the same format as the input file. Each format supports adjustable quality from 10% to 100% for fine-grained control over file size vs. quality.

Web Optimized: 80% quality, max 1200px — ideal for website images. Print Ready: 100% quality, max 3000px — best for physical printing. E-Commerce: 85% quality, white background, 1000px — for product listings. Thumbnail: 60% quality, max 300px — for small previews.

bulk-processor.q: Can I see how much space I saved?
bulk-processor.a: Yes. After processing, each file shows its before/after size and the compression ratio saved. The stats bar shows total original size, total processed size, and total savings — so you can quantify exactly how much space you saved.

bulk-processor.q: Is this tool free to use?
bulk-processor.a: Yes, completely free. No registration, no API keys, no hidden limits. All processing runs locally in your browser with no server-side processing.

heic-to-jpg.q: Is HEIC the same as HEIF?
heic-to-jpg.a: Yes. HEIC is the container, HEIF is the image format.

heic-to-jpg.q: Will the converted JPG look the same?
heic-to-jpg.a: At 90%+ quality, the JPG is visually identical to the original HEIC.

heic-to-jpg.q: Are my photos uploaded to a server?
heic-to-jpg.a: No. HEIC decoding happens in your browser.

ico-icon-generator.q: What's the difference between this and the Favicon Generator?
ico-icon-generator.a: Favicon Generator is for web (fixed sizes + HTML snippet). ICO Icon Generator is for desktop/app icons (custom sizes).
No. Everything runs in your browser using the Canvas API.

ico-icon-generator.q: Does the ICO file use the modern PNG-embedded format?
ico-icon-generator.a: Yes. Each entry inside the .ico container is a full PNG payload.

id-photo.q: Is this ID photo maker really free?
id-photo.a: Yes — completely free with no usage limits, no watermarks, and no registration required. You can generate as many ID photos as you need. All processing runs in your browser using WebAssembly technology — there are no server-side costs because your data never leaves your device.

id-photo.q: Can I use this for official passport applications?
id-photo.a: The tool produces photos meeting the size, aspect ratio, and background color requirements of most countries. However, we recommend double-checking your specific country's passport photo guidelines before submitting, as requirements can vary by issuing office. Some countries have strict rules about photo paper type, ink quality, border thickness, and whether the photo can be self-printed versus professionally printed.

id-photo.q: How does the AI background removal work?
id-photo.a: It uses the imgly background removal model — a state-of-the-art AI neural network that runs entirely in your browser via WebAssembly and ONNX runtime. The AI has been trained on millions of images to accurately detect and separate human subjects from backgrounds. Processing happens locally on your device, so your photo never leaves your computer. No data is sent to any external server.

id-photo.q: What file format and resolution does the output use?
id-photo.a: The output is a high-resolution PNG file rendered at 300 DPI (dots per inch). PNG format ensures lossless quality and preserves fine details needed for official ID photos. The dimensions match the selected country standard at 300 DPI — for example, a US passport photo (51×51 mm at 300 DPI) is 602×602 pixels. The file is suitable for both digital uploads to online application portals and for printing at any photo kiosk or home printer.

id-photo.q: Do you offer the country standard I need?
id-photo.a: We currently support 30+ countries and all major ID photo sizes. If your specific country or document type is not listed, select the "Custom Size" option at the bottom of the country list and enter the width and height in millimeters. The tool will crop and render at your custom dimensions with the selected background color.

id-photo.q: Can I make multiple ID photos for different countries?
id-photo.a: Absolutely. You can select different countries and photo types, change background colors, and generate as many versions as you need — all from the same uploaded photo. Each generation creates a new output with the selected country standards and background color. There are no limits on the number of photos you can generate.

image-compare.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
image-compare.a: No. All image loading and comparison happens entirely in your browser. Your images never leave your device.

image-compare.q: What is the best mode for compression comparison?
image-compare.a: The Slider mode is best — drag the slider slowly across details to see exactly where quality was lost during compression.

image-compare.q: Can I compare images of different sizes?
image-compare.a: Yes, but for the best experience, the images are displayed at their natural size. In Slider and Overlay modes, Image B is scaled to match Image A's dimensions.
Yes, click "Download Comparison" to save a side-by-side PNG of both images. This is useful for sharing or documenting before/after results.
We support JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, and BMP for input. The downloaded comparison is always PNG format.

image-compare.q: Is there a file size limit?
image-compare.a: There is no hard limit, but very large images (over 5000px wide) may be slow to render. For best performance, resize large images before comparing.

image-compare.q: Can I use this for commercial projects?
image-compare.a: Absolutely. The output images are yours to use for any purpose — personal or commercial.

image-compressor.q: What's the difference between this and the Compressor?
image-compressor.a: This is for bulk processing. The single-image Compressor has before/after preview.
For JPG/WebP, yes. The quality slider lets you control the trade-off.

image-compressor.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?

image-filters.q: Is my image uploaded to a server?
image-filters.a: No. All filtering happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device. There is no server that receives or stores your files.
We support JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, and BMP for input. You can download the result as PNG, JPG, or WebP.
Yes! The preset filters and slider adjustments are applied together. The Canvas filter property combines all effects in a single pass. Click a preset, then adjust sliders to create your custom look.
No. Filters are applied by the browser's Canvas rendering engine without re-compressing your image. For best quality, download as PNG format.

image-filters.q: Which preset filter is best for portraits?
image-filters.a: The Warm filter is flattering for skin tones. For a classic look, try Vintage. For a modern, crisp look, apply the Vibrant preset and reduce saturation slightly with the slider.

image-filters.q: Can I use this for commercial projects?
image-filters.a: Absolutely. The output images are yours to use for any purpose — personal or commercial. No watermarks, no attribution required.

image-filters.q: Why do colors look different after downloading?
image-filters.a: This can happen due to color space differences between browsers and image viewers. For consistent colors, use PNG format and view in a color-managed application like Photoshop or modern browsers.

image-merger.q: Is there a limit on how many images I can merge?
image-merger.a: There's no hard limit, but we recommend merging up to 20 images for best performance. Very large collages may slow down the browser preview. The final output resolution depends on your input images and the number of items.

image-merger.q: Will my images be uploaded to a server?
image-merger.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device. No server ever receives or stores your photos.

image-merger.q: Can I merge images of different sizes?
image-merger.a: Yes. In Grid mode, images are resized to fit equal cells. In Horizontal mode, all images are scaled to the same height. In Vertical mode, all images are scaled to the same width. The tool handles different sizes automatically.
Simply drag and drop the image thumbnails in the sidebar list. The preview updates instantly to reflect the new order.

The output resolution depends on your input images and layout. Grid mode calculates cell size based on the largest image. Horizontal and Vertical modes preserve the original resolution of the first image as the reference. Very large outputs may be limited by browser canvas constraints.

image-merger.q: Can I remove an image after uploading?
image-merger.a: Yes. Each image in the sidebar has an "×" button. Click it to remove that image from the collage. You can also add more images at any time.

image-merger.q: Does the tool work on mobile?
image-merger.a: Yes. The interface is fully responsive. On mobile devices, the sidebar and canvas stack vertically. Touch-based reordering is also supported.

image-rotator.a: 90° and 180° rotations are lossless — pixels are simply rearranged. Custom angle rotations use high-quality bicubic interpolation, which may introduce very slight softening at extreme angles. For most purposes, the quality is excellent.

image-rotator.q: Will my image be uploaded to a server?
image-rotator.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device. There is no server that receives or stores your files.

image-rotator.q: What happens to the canvas size when I rotate?
image-rotator.a: For 90° and 270° rotations, the canvas width and height swap to fit the rotated image perfectly. For custom angles, the canvas expands to contain the entire rotated image, and the background color fills any new space.

image-rotator.q: Can I rotate and flip at the same time?
image-rotator.a: Yes. Set your rotation angle first, then click a flip button. The flip applies on top of the current rotation. Both transformations are combined in the final output.

image-rotator.q: What's the difference between rotating 180° and flipping vertically?
image-rotator.a: Rotating 180° turns the image upside down (top becomes bottom, left becomes right). Flipping vertically only mirrors top-to-bottom (left stays left). They produce different results unless the image is perfectly symmetrical.
You can upload a GIF, but only the first frame will be rotated. The output will be a static image (PNG, JPG, or WebP), not an animated GIF. For animated GIF rotation, a specialized tool is needed.

image-rotator.q: Is there a file size limit?
image-rotator.a: There's no artificial limit, but very large images (over 50 megapixels) may be slow to process in the browser. Most photos from phones and cameras work instantly.

image-upscaler.q: How is this different from simply resizing?
image-upscaler.a: Regular resizing uses basic interpolation which produces blurry results. Our upscaler uses high-quality bicubic interpolation combined with a sharpening filter that enhances edges and restores detail clarity. The result is noticeably crisper than a simple resize.

image-upscaler.q: Will my image be uploaded to a server?
image-upscaler.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device. No server ever receives or stores your files.

image-upscaler.q: Can I upscale to a custom scale factor?
image-upscaler.a: Currently we support 2x, 3x, and 4x as these are the most commonly needed factors. If you need a specific size, try using our Image Resizer tool after upscaling to get the exact dimensions you need.

Upscaling cannot create detail that doesn't exist in the original image. What it does is intelligently interpolate between existing pixels and apply sharpening to maintain the perception of sharpness. The result looks better than a simple resize, but won't match a natively high-resolution photo.

image-upscaler.q: What is the sharpening filter doing?
image-upscaler.a: The sharpening filter is an unsharp mask technique that enhances edge contrast. It works by subtracting a blurred version of the image from the original, which makes edges appear crisper. The slider controls the intensity of this effect.

image-upscaler.q: Is there a file size or resolution limit?
image-upscaler.a: There's no artificial limit, but very large outputs (e.g., 4x on a 5000px image = 20000px) may be slow or run into browser memory constraints. Most typical photo upscales complete in seconds.

image-upscaler.q: Should I use PNG or JPG for upscaled images?
image-upscaler.a: Use PNG for images with sharp edges (logos, screenshots, text) or when quality is paramount. Use JPG for photographs where file size matters more than pixel-perfect accuracy. WebP is a good modern alternative that balances both.

meme-generator.q: Is my image uploaded to a server?
meme-generator.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser. Your images never leave your device.
Drake, Distracted Boyfriend, Woman Yelling at Cat, Two Buttons, and Custom (upload your own). More templates are coming soon!

meme-generator.q: Can I use my own image as a template?
meme-generator.a: Yes! Click the upload area or drag and drop any image. It will be used as the meme background, and you can add top/bottom text to it.

meme-generator.q: What is the best font size?
meme-generator.a: The default 60px works well for most standard memes. For tall images, increase to 80-100px. For wide images with short text, 40-50px may look better. Always preview before downloading.

meme-generator.q: Why does my text look blurry?
meme-generator.a: This can happen if the canvas is very large and the font size is small. Try increasing the font size slider, or use a taller image template.

meme-generator.q: Can I use this for commercial purposes?
meme-generator.a: You retain full rights to memes you create. Note: some meme templates may be copyrighted images — for commercial use, use your own images or properly licensed templates.

meme-generator.q: What output format should I use?
meme-generator.a: PNG is recommended for maximum quality and sharp text. JPG produces smaller files but may introduce compression artifacts around high-contrast text. WebP is a good modern alternative with excellent compression.

photo-restoration.q: Is this photo restoration tool free?
photo-restoration.a: Yes — 100% free. All processing runs in your browser with no limits, no signup, and no server uploads. There are no hidden charges, watermarks, or usage caps.
JPG, PNG, WebP, and most browser-supported image formats. The restored photo is downloaded as a high-quality PNG file (lossless).

photo-restoration.q: Does this tool use AI or machine learning?
photo-restoration.a: No. All restoration is done using pure Canvas image processing algorithms — median filter denoising, convolution-based sharpening, histogram stretching, and adaptive pixel analysis for scratch removal. No external AI models, APIs, or cloud services are used. Everything runs entirely in your browser.
Absolutely. Your image never leaves your browser. No uploads, no tracking cookies, no server processing. Your old family photos stay on your computer.

photo-restoration.q: What is the maximum image size I can upload?
photo-restoration.a: Images up to 20MB are supported. Very large images (e.g., high-resolution scans at 1200+ DPI) may process more slowly because all computation happens locally in your browser's JavaScript engine.

photo-restoration.q: Can I restore color in old black and white photos?
photo-restoration.a: This tool does not perform AI colorization (which requires external ML models). However, you can use the Warmth/Sepia slider (0–100) to add a warm vintage sepia tone that gives old black-and-white photos a classic antique look. Start at 40–60 for authentic sepia.

photo-restoration.q: What is the best way to scan old photos for restoration?
photo-restoration.a: For best results: scan at 600 DPI or higher using a flatbed scanner. Avoid using phone cameras with flash (creates glare). Save as PNG (lossless) or high-quality JPEG. Clean the photo gently with a microfiber cloth before scanning. Handle old photos by the edges.

print-resizer.q: What DPI should I use for photo prints?
print-resizer.a: 300 DPI is the industry standard for high-quality photo prints. Most photo labs require 300 DPI. For large-format prints (posters, banners) viewed from >3m away, 150 DPI is acceptable.

print-resizer.q: What is the difference between A4 and Letter?
print-resizer.a: A4 (210×297mm) is the international standard used in most countries. Letter (8.5×11 inches / 216×279mm) is the US standard. Always check which your print service expects.

print-resizer.q: My image is too small for 300 DPI — what should I do?
print-resizer.a: If your source image has fewer pixels than the target DPI size, use our Image Upscaler tool first to enlarge it 2× or 4×, then come back to set the correct DPI.

print-resizer.q: Should I download as PNG or JPG?
print-resizer.a: For photos, JPG at quality 92+ is fine and produces smaller files. For text, line art, screenshots, or images with sharp edges, use PNG to avoid compression artifacts.

print-resizer.q: Does this actually embed the DPI in the file?
print-resizer.a: Yes. The Canvas API produces images with the correct pixel dimensions for the chosen DPI and paper size. When you open the file in Photoshop or your print lab's upload system, the dimensions will match the physical print size at the specified DPI.

print-resizer.q: Can I use this for commercial printing?
print-resizer.a: Yes. The output images are print-ready. For commercial printing, we recommend 300 DPI and JPG format (the industry standard). Always request a proof before a large print run.

print-resizer.q: Is my image uploaded to a server?
print-resizer.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser. Your images never leave your device.

product-white-background.q: Why do e-commerce products need a white background?
product-white-background.a: Many online marketplaces like Amazon, eBay, and Google Shopping require or recommend pure white backgrounds (#ffffff) for product images. White backgrounds make products stand out, look professional, and ensure consistency across listings. Amazon's main image requirements specifically mandate a pure white background for the primary product photo.

product-white-background.q: How accurate is the automatic background removal?
product-white-background.a: For most product photos with clear subjects and contrasting backgrounds, the AI achieves 95%+ accuracy. The model performs best on products with distinct edges like electronics, shoes, bottles, and packaged goods. Products with fine details like hair, fur, or transparent elements may need manual touch-up in an external editor.

product-white-background.q: Are my product images uploaded to a server?
product-white-background.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using WebAssembly AI technology. Your product images never leave your device. This makes it completely private and secure, ideal for confidential product photography before an official launch.

product-white-background.q: How many product photos can I process at once?
product-white-background.a: You can process any number of images in a batch. Your browser's memory is the only limit. For large batches, we recommend processing 20-30 images at a time for optimal performance. All images in the batch are processed with a single click.

product-white-background.q: What image formats are supported for product photos?
product-white-background.a: This tool supports JPG, PNG, and WebP formats. Processed images are saved as PNG to preserve the transparent background information. PNG format also maintains the highest quality for e-commerce product images.

product-white-background.q: Can I use the white background photos for Amazon listings?
product-white-background.a: Yes. Amazon requires the main product image to have a pure white background (#ffffff) that seamlessly blends with the page. Our tool outputs images with exact #ffffff white backgrounds, fully compatible with Amazon, eBay, Shopify, Etsy, and other major e-commerce platforms. The processed images use PNG format for best quality.

qr-code-generator.q: Is this QR code generator really free?
qr-code-generator.a: Yes, completely free with no usage limits and no watermarks.

qr-code-generator.q: Is my data uploaded to a server?
qr-code-generator.a: No. All QR generation happens locally in your browser.

qr-code-generator.q: What error correction level should I use?
qr-code-generator.a: Use M (15%) for clean prints. Use Q or H when adding a center logo.

screenshot-to-image.q: Is my screenshot uploaded to a server?
screenshot-to-image.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your screenshots never leave your device. There is no server that receives or stores your files.

The output resolution depends on your input screenshot and the padding settings. The tool generates a high-resolution image at 1x pixel density. For retina-quality output, upload a high-resolution screenshot.

screenshot-to-image.q: Can I customize the gradient colors?
screenshot-to-image.a: Yes! We offer 10 curated gradient presets, and you can also use the custom background color picker to set any solid color. For full gradient customization, pick a preset that's close to what you want and adjust.

screenshot-to-image.q: What is the browser frame style?
screenshot-to-image.a: The Browser frame adds a macOS-style window title bar above your screenshot, complete with red, yellow, and green traffic light buttons and a thin address bar. It makes web screenshots instantly recognizable as websites.

screenshot-to-image.q: Can I use this for commercial projects?
screenshot-to-image.a: Absolutely. The output images are yours to use for any purpose — personal or commercial. There are no watermarks, no attribution requirements, and no usage restrictions.

screenshot-to-image.q: What image formats are supported for input?
screenshot-to-image.a: We support JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, and BMP for input. The tool works best with PNG screenshots for maximum quality, but any standard image format will work.

screenshot-to-image.q: How do I get the best-looking result?
screenshot-to-image.a: Use a high-resolution screenshot (at least 1280px wide), add generous padding (64-100px), choose a gradient that complements your screenshot's color scheme, and add a subtle shadow (30-50px blur, 20-30% opacity). These settings create a professional, polished look.

social-media-post.q: Is this social media post maker really free?
social-media-post.a: Yes — 100% free. No signup, no watermarks, no hidden charges. All processing runs in your browser and your images never leave your computer.

social-media-post.q: What social media platforms does this tool support?
social-media-post.a: It supports Instagram (Post & Story), Facebook (Post & Cover), Twitter/X (Post & Header), LinkedIn (Post & Banner), YouTube (Thumbnail & Channel Art), TikTok Video, Pinterest Pin, and any custom size you specify.

social-media-post.q: Can I add custom fonts or use my brand colors?
social-media-post.a: You can set any text color using the color picker, choose font size, and pick text alignment. For brand colors, use the hex code or picker to match exactly.

social-media-post.q: Can I reposition text and images after placing them?
social-media-post.a: Yes. You can adjust the vertical Y offset of text and overlay images using the sliders. The canvas updates in real-time so you can fine-tune positioning.

social-media-post.q: Will my designs lose quality when I download?
social-media-post.a: No. Your design is rendered at the full platform resolution (e.g. 1080×1080 for Instagram, 1280×720 for YouTube) and downloaded as a lossless PNG file.
Absolutely. All compositing is done locally in your browser. No images or text are uploaded to any server. Your designs stay on your device.

svg-to-png.q: Is my SVG uploaded to a server?
svg-to-png.a: No. All conversion happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your SVG file or code never leaves your device.

svg-to-png.q: What is the maximum SVG size supported?
svg-to-png.a: There is no hard file size limit. However, very large SVGs (e.g., 2000×2000+ pixels at 4x scale) may take longer to render. Most SVGs under 1MB convert instantly.

svg-to-png.q: Why does my converted image look different from the SVG?
svg-to-png.a: This can happen if your SVG uses external resources (linked images, fonts) or CSS styles not embedded in the SVG. For best results, use self-contained SVG code with embedded fonts or convert fonts to paths in your design tool before exporting.

svg-to-png.q: Can I convert animated SVGs (SVG + SMIL)?
svg-to-png.a: Animated SVGs will be converted at their initial static state. The Canvas API renders a single frame. For animated outputs, consider exporting individual frames from your animation tool.

svg-to-png.q: What scale factor should I use for web use?
svg-to-png.a: Use 2x scale for most web use — this ensures crisp display on retina/ high-DPI screens. Use 1x for standard displays, or 3-4x for print.

svg-to-png.q: Can I use the output for commercial projects?
svg-to-png.a: Yes. The output images are yours to use for any purpose. Note that font licensing may apply if your SVG uses embedded commercial fonts — check your font license.

svg-to-png.q: Does this support SVG filters and effects?
svg-to-png.a: Yes, most SVG filters (blur, drop shadow, color matrix) and effects are supported as long as the browser's SVG renderer supports them. Modern Chrome, Firefox, and Safari have excellent SVG support.

text-on-image.q: Can I add multiple text elements?
text-on-image.a: Currently, the tool supports one text element per image. For multiple text layers, you can download the result and upload it again to add a second text element. We're considering multi-text support in a future update.

text-on-image.q: Will my image be uploaded to a server?
text-on-image.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images and text never leave your device. There is no server that receives or stores your files.

We offer 10 curated Google Fonts that cover a wide range of styles. Custom font uploads aren't currently supported, but we've selected fonts that work well for most use cases — from professional to decorative.

text-on-image.q: How do I position the text precisely?
text-on-image.a: You can drag the text directly on the preview canvas. For quick placement, use the 9-position grid in the sidebar. For pixel-perfect positioning, zoom in on the canvas and drag slowly.

text-on-image.q: Does the outline work with transparent text?
text-on-image.a: Yes! You can set the text color to any value, including colors with the opacity slider. The outline is drawn separately, so it will still appear even when the text fill is semi-transparent.

text-on-image.q: What's the best text style for memes?
text-on-image.a: Use white text, black outline (3-5px width), Impact or Bebas Neue font, bold weight, and large size (60-100px). Position at top or bottom of the image. This is the classic meme format that's instantly recognizable.

text-on-image.q: Can I use this for multiline text?
text-on-image.a: Yes. Type your text with line breaks in the text area, and each line will be rendered separately on the canvas with consistent spacing. This is useful for quotes or multi-line captions.
